Rashi on Berakhot 12a:10:1.hebrew: פתח בדשכרא וסיים בדחמרא - תחלת הברכה אמר ע"מ שהכל, וכיון שהגיע למלך העולם נזכר שהוא יין ואמר פרי הגפן. פשיטא לן דיצא — דהא אפילו סיים כל הברכה כדעת פתיחתה ואמר שהכל, יצא על היין, דתנן וכו':
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:10:1.english: [If] he began with beer and concluded with wine - He recited the beginning of the blessing with the intention of [saying] Shehakol [By Whose word all things came to be], and once he reached "King of the universe," he remembered that it was wine and said "[Who creates] the fruit of the vine." It is obvious to us that he has fulfilled [his obligation], for even had he completed the entire blessing in accordance with the intention of its opening and said Shehakol, he would have fulfilled [his obligation] for the wine, as we learned [in the mishna: "Over all of them..."] etc.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:11:1.hebrew: אלא - קא מבעיא לן: פתח אדעתא דחמרא כדי לסיים בפה"ג, וכשהגיע למלך העולם נזכר שהוא שכר, וסיים שהכל — מהו:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:11:1.english: However - It is a dilemma for us: [If] he began with the intention of [blessing over] wine, in order to conclude with "Who creates the fruit of the vine," and when he reached "King of the Universe" he remembered that it was beer, and concluded with "by Whose word all things came to be" — what is [the halakha]?

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:12:1.hebrew: בתר עיקר ברכה אזלינן - ועיקר ברכה אדעתא דיין נאמרה, והוי כמו שסיים ביין, ואין ברכת היין מוציאה ידי ברכת שכר, שאין השכר מן הגפן:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:12:1.english: Do we follow the essence of the blessing - And the essence of the blessing was recited with wine in mind, and it is as though he concluded with wine, and the blessing over wine does not fulfill the obligation for the blessing over beer, for beer is not from the vine.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:13:1.hebrew: פתח ביוצר אור - כלומר, אדעתא דלימא יוצר אור:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:13:1.english: [If] he began with “Who creates light” - That is to say, with the intention to say “Who creates light.”

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:13:2.hebrew: וסיים במעריב ערבים - כשאמר מלך העולם, נזכר וסיים אשר בדברו מעריב ערבים:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:13:2.english: And concluded with “Who brings on evenings” - When he said “King of the Universe,” he remembered and concluded, “Who by His word brings on evenings.”

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:16:1.hebrew: שאני התם וכו' - כלומר, דלמא פתיחה אינה כלום, והא דקתני יצא, לפי שחוזר וחותם בה בברוך יוצר המאורות, וע"י חתימתה קאמר דיצא. אלא שהכל, שאין חותם בה בברוך, ופתיחתה אדעתא דבורא פרי הגפן הוא — אימא דלא יצא:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:16:1.english: There it is different, etc. - That is to say, perhaps the opening [of a blessing] is of no account, and that which [the baraita] teaches, '[he has] fulfilled [his obligation],' is because he goes back and concludes it with 'Blessed... Who forms the radiant lights,' and on account of its conclusion it says that he has fulfilled [his obligation]. Whereas [in the case of] *Shehakol*, where one does not conclude it with 'Blessed,' and its opening was with the intention of [reciting] 'Who creates the fruit of the vine' — say that he has not fulfilled [his obligation].

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:17:1.hebrew: מאי איכא למימר - היכי נפיק משום חתימתה? הא אין מלכות בחתימתה:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:17:1.english: What can be said - How does he fulfill [his obligation] through its conclusion? Behold, there is no [mention of] sovereignty in its conclusion.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:18:1.hebrew: ה"ג אלא כיון דאמר כו' - אלא — לא תימא משום חתימתה יצא, אלא פתיחתה נמי מעלייתא היא, ולא תפשוט מיניה לחמרא ושכרא. דלגבי ברכות ערבית ושחרית הוא דמצי למימר דכי פתח בזו וסיים בזו יצא, דהא כי פתח בשחרית אדעתא דמעריב ערבים, הוה דעתיה לאדכורי בה מדת היום בלילה, כגון גולל אור; וכי פתח ערבית אדעתא דיוצר אור, הוה דעתיה לאדכורי בה מדת לילה, כגון ובורא חשך. הלכך, אדעתא דתרוייהו הויא:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:18:1.english: This is our reading: Rather, since [Rabba bar Ulla] said, etc. - "Rather" — do not say that he fulfilled [his obligation] because of its conclusion; rather, its opening is also proper, and do not resolve from this [the dilemma regarding] wine and beer. For it is [only] with regard to the blessings of the evening and morning [services] that one can say that when he opened with this [one] and concluded with that [one], he fulfilled [his obligation]; for when he opened in the morning [service] with the intention of [reciting] Maariv Aravim, his intention was to mention in it the attribute of day at night, such as [the phrase] "Who rolls away light"; and when he opened in the evening [service] with the intention of [reciting] Yotzer Or, his intention was to mention in it the attribute of night, such as [the phrase] "and creates darkness." Therefore, it was [recited] with the intention of both.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:19:1.hebrew: לאו לאתויי הא דאמרן - כגון שכרא וחמרא:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:19:1.english: Does it not come to include that which we said - Such as [the case of] beer and wine.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:1:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת - הך ברכה דקאמרי אהבה רבה, היכי ש"מ דאין מעכבות זו את זו? דלמא האי דלא אמרי יוצר אור משום דלא מטא זמניה הוא, וכי מטא זמניה אמרי לה. ואע"ג דקרו אינהו ק"ש, לא מטא זמניה, כדאמרינן בעלמא (יומא לז:): הקורא את שמע עם אנשי משמר לא יצא, שאנשי משמר מקדימין:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:1:1.english: Rather, if you say - [That] that blessing which they recited was Ahavah Rabbah — how do you infer from this that [the blessings] do not prevent one another? Perhaps the reason that they did not recite Yotzer Or was because its time had not yet arrived, and when its time arrived, they would recite it. And even though they had recited the Shema, its time had not [yet] arrived, as we say elsewhere (Yoma 37b): “One who recites the Shema with the men of the priestly watch has not fulfilled [his obligation], for the men of the priestly watch recite [it] early.”

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:20:1.hebrew: היינו בעיין - דהא ברכת התמרים — על העץ ועל פרי העץ — אינה עולה לברכת הלחם. ואי בהא פשטת דהכל הולך אחר חתום ברכות, הוא הדין לחמרא ושכרא:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:20:1.english: Isn’t that our dilemma - For the blessing over dates — “On the tree and on the fruit of the tree” — does not count toward the blessing over bread. And if in this [case] you resolve that everything follows the conclusion of blessings, the same law applies to wine and beer.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:23:1.hebrew: כל מי - שלא אמר ברכת אמת ויציב כמו שתקנוה, וכן אמת ואמונה בערבית — לא יצא:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:23:1.english: Whoever - [One] who did not recite the blessing of Emet Veyatziv as [the Sages] instituted it, and likewise [the blessing of] Emet Ve’emuna in the evening, has not fulfilled [his obligation].

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:23:2.hebrew: שנא' להגיד בבקר חסדך - וברכת אמת ויציב כולה על חסד שעשה עם אבותינו היא, שהוציאם ממצרים ובקע להם הים והעבירם. וברכת אמת ואמונה מדבר בה אף על העתידות, שאנו מצפים שיקיים לנו הבטחתו ואמונתו, לגאלנו מיד מלכים ומיד עריצים, ולשום נפשנו בחיים, ולהדריכנו על במות אויבינו — כל אלה הנסים התדירים תמיד:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:23:2.english: As it is stated: “To declare Your kindness in the morning” - And the blessing of Emet Veyatziv is entirely about the kindness that He performed for our ancestors, in that He brought them out of Egypt, split the sea for them, and brought them across. And the blessing of Emet Ve’emuna speaks also of the future, as we look forward to His fulfilling His promise and His faithfulness to us: to redeem us from the hand of kings and from the hand of tyrants, and to preserve our souls in life, and to cause us to tread upon the high places of our enemies — all these miracles that are constantly recurring.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:24:1.hebrew: כשהוא כורע - באבות ובהודאה — כורע בברוך, וזוקף את עצמו כשהוא מזכיר את השם, על שם "ה' זוקף כפופים" (תהילים קמ״ו:ח׳):
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:24:1.english: When he bows - In [the blessings of] the Patriarchs [Avot] and Thanksgiving [Hoda'ah] — he bows at [the word] "Blessed," and straightens himself when he mentions the Name [of God], based on [the verse]: "The Lord straightens the bowed" (Psalms 146:8).

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:26:1.english: [He] was humbled - An expression of submission.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:2:1.hebrew: ואי מכללא מאי - וכי אמר ליה מכללא, מאי גריעותא איכא דאמר: "לאו בפירוש אתמר"? הא שפיר מצי למשמע מכללא דיוצר אור קא אמרי. ומשנינן: ליכא למשמע מהכא, דילמא לעולם אימא לך אהבה רבה וכו':
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:2:1.english: And if [it is] based on an inference, what of it - Even if he said to him [that it was derived] from an inference, what deficiency is there [in that], that he said, "It was not stated explicitly"? Behold, one can well deduce from the inference that they recited "Who creates light"! And we answer: It cannot be deduced from here, for perhaps I could always say to you [that they recited] "An abounding love," etc.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:3:1.english: The order of the blessings - If one recited the latter [blessings] first.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:5:1.hebrew: בקשו - לקבוע עשרת הדברות בקריאת שמע:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:5:1.english: They sought - To establish the Ten Commandments in the recitation of the Shema.

Rashi on Berakhot 12a:5:2.hebrew: מפני תרעומת המינין - שלא יאמרו לעמי הארץ: אין שאר תורה אמת, ותדעו שאין קורין אלא מה שאמר הקדוש ב"ה ושמעו מפיו בסיני:
Rashi on Berakhot 12a:5:2.english: Due to the grievance of the heretics - Lest they say to the common people: "The rest of the Torah is not true, and know [that this is so, for] they only recite what the Holy One, blessed be He, said and they heard from His mouth at Sinai."

Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:11:1.hebrew: פתח - ואמר בא"י אלהינו מלך העולם, והיה סבור שהיה יין, והבין שהיה שכר, ואחר שהבין שהיה שכר — סיים שהכל:
Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:11:1.english: "He opened" - And he said: "Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe," and he thought that it was wine, and realized that it was beer; and after realizing that it was beer, he concluded [with] "by Whose word all things came to be."

Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:1:1.hebrew: משום דלא מטא זמן יוצר אור - דנהי דשחיטת התמיד משיעלה עמוד השחר, פי' רש"י: מיהו לא הוה שעה לומר "יוצר אור", כדאמרי': "הקורא כו'". ויכול לסבור הברייתא כותיקין:
Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:1:1.english: "Because the time for [the blessing of] Who creates light had not yet arrived" - For granted that the slaughter of the daily morning offering is from when dawn rises, Rashi explained: nevertheless, it was not yet the time to recite "Who creates light", as we say: "One who recites [the Shema with the members of the priestly watch has not fulfilled his obligation...]" And [one] can maintain that the baraita [holds] in accordance with the vatikin.

Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:20:1.hebrew: לא לאתויי נהמא - ופירש רב אלפס: השתא דלא אפשיטא בעיין, אזלינן לקולא, ואפילו פתח בחמרא וסיים בשכרא — יצא. ור"י הי' אומר לחומרא: דצריך לברך פעם אחרת. ומיהו, היה אומר ר"ח: אם היה יודע בבירור שטעה בדבורו, שאמר בורא פרי העץ תחת (בורא) פרי הגפן — דבתוך כדי דבור יכול לחזור בו. וכן בי"ט, בחתימה של יום טוב: אם טעה בין מקדש ישראל והזמנים ואמר מקדש השבת, וחזר בתוך כדי דבור — יצא, אחרי שהוא יודע שהוא י"ט. והקשה הר"ר יעקב מקינון: מאי קא מבעיא ליה, והא ודאי מצות אינן צריכות כוונה? והיה אומר הר"י: דהיינו בשומע תפלה אחורי בית הכנסת ולא נתכוין לצאת, אבל היכא דנתכוין לברך על היין ונמצא שכר — לא מהני:
Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:20:1.english: "No, to include bread" - And Rav Alfas explained: Now that our dilemma was not resolved, we follow the lenient [course], and even if one began [intending the blessing] for wine and concluded with [the blessing for] beer, he has fulfilled [his obligation]. And the Ri would say stringently that one must recite a blessing another time. However, Rabbeinu Ḥananel would say: If he knew with certainty that he had erred in his speech, in that he said "Who creates the fruit of the tree" instead of "(Who creates) the fruit of the vine," within the time required for an utterance [tokh kedei dibbur] he can retract [and correct it]. And similarly on a Festival, in the conclusion of [the blessing of] the Festival: if he erred regarding "Who sanctifies Israel and the festive seasons" and said "Who sanctifies the Shabbat," and corrected himself within the time required for an utterance [tokh kedei dibbur], he has fulfilled [his obligation], since he knows that it is a Festival. And Rabbi Jacob of Chinon raised a difficulty: What was the dilemma for [the Gemara]? For surely mitzvot do not require intention! And the Ri would say: That is [only] in [the case of] one who hears prayer behind the synagogue and did not intend to fulfill [his obligation]; but where one intended to recite a blessing over wine and it turned out to be beer, it is not effective.

Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:23:1.hebrew: אמת ויציב וכו' - לא קאי על השכינה, אלא קאי אהדבר הזה וכו'. וכן איתא בהר"ם. ואיתא בירושלמי: "האי מרגניתא דלית ביה טימא" — פירוש: שאין לה שומא — "כל מה שמשבח מתגני לה", כדאמר לקמן (ברכות ד' לג ב) בחד דפתח ואמר: "האל הגדול הגבור והנורא", והיה מאריך הרבה, וא"ל ר' חנינא: "סיימת לשבחי דמרך?!" — כי כל פה לא יוכל לספר שבחו:
Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:23:1.english: "True and firm," etc. - [This] does not refer to the Divine Presence [the Shekhina], but rather refers to "this matter, etc." [in the blessing: "this matter is true and firm upon us forever and ever"]. And so it is found in [the writings of] the Rav, Rabbi Moses [Maimonides]. And it is found in the Yerushalmi: "This pearl that has no tima" — explanation: that has no appraisal [it is priceless] — "the more one praises it, the more it is demeaned," as [the Gemara] says later (Berakhot 33b) regarding a certain [individual] who began and said: "The great, the mighty, and the awesome God," and was elaborating greatly, and Rabbi Ḥanina said to him: "Have you concluded the praises of your Master?!" — for no mouth can recount His praise.

Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:23:2.hebrew: להגיד בבקר חסדך - חסד שהקדוש ב"ה עשה לנו במצרים. "ואמונתך" — פי': מדבר על העתיד, שאנו מצפים שישמור הבטחתו ואמונתו ויגאלנו מיד המלכים. ובסוף ברכה חוזר לגאולה דפרעה, כדי לסמוך ל"גאל ישראל". א"נ ע"ד המדר' (רבה איכה ג): "חדשים לבקרים רבה אמונתך" — שאדם מאמין ומפקיד רוחו בידו, ומחזירה בלא יגיעה:
Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:23:2.english: “To declare Your kindness in the morning” - [This refers to the] kindness that the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for us in Egypt. And “and Your faithfulness” — explanation: [the blessing] speaks of the future, as we look forward to His keeping His promise and His faithfulness, and redeeming us from the hand of the kings. And at the end of the blessing, [the blessing] returns to the redemption of Pharaoh in order to juxtapose [it] to “Who redeemed Israel.” Alternatively, [it is] in the manner of the Midrash (Eikha Rabbah 3) [on the verse]: “They are new every morning; great is Your faithfulness” — that a person has faith and entrusts his spirit into His hand, and He returns it without weariness.

Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:9:1.hebrew: ברכה אחת למשמר היוצא וכו' - תימא קצת: מאי היא, הואיל ולית בה לא שם ולא מלכות:
Tosafot on Berakhot 12a:9:1.english: "A single blessing for the outgoing priestly watch," etc. - It is somewhat surprising: what [kind of blessing] is it, since it contains neither [the Divine] Name nor [mention of Divine] sovereignty?
